correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed from the transform definition. A fixed point must be absolutely continuous; its CDF satisfies the two linear first-order equations almost everywhere, which integrate uniquely on the two half-lines. Continuity at zero joins the side masses, and direct substitution verifies every member of the resulting family. No numerical or finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for a recently introduced probability transform. It identifies the exact structural invariant left by extending equilibrium biasing to both signs: memorylessness survives in the magnitude, while an arbitrary independent sign bias survives as a new degree of freedom. This distinguishes the two-sided transform from classical one-sided fixed-point uniqueness and supplies a reusable benchmark for future transform or approximation results.
